evidence_set: 118 RCTs (156 articles, 20,976 participants), 81 of them carried over from the 2014 review; all participants met criteria for alcohol dependence in 103 of 118 trials; 87 (73.7%) of 118 included a psychosocial co-intervention; mean age was typically 40 to 49 years, and 63 of the 70 trials reporting race and sex enrolled mostly White men. Of 49 naltrexone trials, 32 were in the US and 8 in Europe.

The review's judgments of its 50 trials: sequence generation adequately described in 14, allocation concealment adequate in 3, blinding adequate in 21; missing binary data handled adequately in 11 of 40. evidence_set: Against placebo: topiramate, percentage of drinking days WMD −7.2 (95% CI −14.3 to −0.1), 8 trials, 1080 participants; percentage of heavy drinking days −6.2 (−10.9 to −1.4), 9 trials, 1210; drinks per drinking day −2.0 (−3.1 to −1.0), 7 trials, 922; all moderate strength of evidence. Baclofen, return to any drinking RR 0.83 (0.70 to 0.98), 8 trials, 995, low (imprecision and inconsistency); its other drinking outcomes and quality of life were graded low strength of evidence for no effect, while crashes or injuries (no trials) and deaths (8 against 3, 4 trials) had insufficient evidence. Gabapentin, return to any drinking 0.92 (0.83 to 1.02) and return to heavy drinking 0.90 (0.82 to 0.98), 3 trials, 522, low. Results are presented for medicines with at least low strength of evidence for benefit for some outcomes; ondansetron, varenicline and prazosin, described as having either low strength of evidence suggesting benefit or insufficient evidence, are not further discussed in the article (supplementary eTable 5).
